title: Speed & rate problems (P6)
examples: When does the faster car catch up to the slower car?
How far apart will two people be after two hours?
What is the average speed if I travel different distances?

explain.say: Today we learn about speed problems. Speed tells us how fast something moves. We use the formula distance equals speed times time.

items: Speed measures how fast something moves.

explain.say: First we look at meeting problems. If two things move toward each other, we add their speeds. This is called the relative speed.

items: Two objects move toward each other

explain.say: The time until they meet is the total distance divided by the combined speed. For example, if they are ten kilometers apart and move together, the time is ten divided by the sum of their speeds.
Next we learn about overtaking. When one thing chases another, we subtract the speeds. This is the difference in speed.

draw.text: Relative Speed = Faster Speed - Slower Speed

explain.say: The time to overtake is the initial gap divided by the difference in speeds. For example, if the gap is twenty kilometers and the difference in speed is five kilometers per hour, the time is twenty divided by five.

draw.text: Time = Initial Gap / (Faster Speed - Slower Speed)

faq.q: If two people are moving in the same direction, do I add or subtract their speeds?
faq.a: You must subtract the speeds to find the relative speed. This tells you how quickly the gap is closing or increasing. You might also ask how fast the faster one is pulling away.
asks: When do I use subtraction for speed?
Should I add or subtract when they go the same way?

faq.q: When I calculate average speed, do I average the speeds?
faq.a: No, you should not average the speeds directly. You must calculate the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. You might also ask for the overall speed.
asks: Is average speed just the middle speed?
How do I find the true average speed?

faq.q: For meeting problems, is the total distance always the starting gap?
faq.a: Yes, the total distance is the initial distance separating the two objects. You use this distance divided by the sum of their speeds. You might also ask for the time to meet.
asks: What distance do I use for meeting problems?
Is the starting distance the key number?

faq.q: If the time changes, does the distance change too?
faq.a: Yes, distance, speed, and time are linked by a formula. If you know two, you can find the third. For example, if time doubles, the distance also doubles if speed stays the same.
asks: If I go faster, what happens to the distance?
How are the three variables connected?

faq.q: Does the unit of speed have to match the unit of distance?
faq.a: Yes, the units must match correctly. If distance is in kilometers, speed must be in kilometers per hour. You might also ask about unit conversion.
asks: What if I have miles and hours?
Do I need to change units first?

facts: Speed is the rate of change of distance over time.
The formula connecting these is distance equals speed times time.
When objects move towards each other, their speeds add up.
Average speed is total distance divided by total time.

quiz.say: A car travels 120 kilometers in 2 hours. What is its speed?
quiz.why: You divide the total distance by the total time, so 120 divided by 2 equals 60.

wrong.0: This mistake occurs if you multiply the distance by the speed.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you multiply the distance by the time, which is incorrect.
wrong.3: This mistake might happen if you only use the first number given.

quiz.say: A train leaves station A for station B, 300 kilometers away. It travels first at 50 kilometers per hour for 2 hours, and then at 100 kilometers per hour for 1 hour. What is the average speed for the whole trip?
quiz.why: The total distance is 200 plus 100, which is 300. The total time is 2 plus 1, which is 3. So, 300 divided by 3 is 60.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you multiply the two speeds together.
wrong.1: This mistake happens if you only use the speed from the second part of the journey.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you average the two speeds, 50 and 100.
